defects_closed.fix: admittedEndpointAddress and admittedLocalOffset with one shared tile-base definition

defects_closed.fix: per-execution observation records plus a per-execution transfer contribution; the lifetime map is now only the transport row

defects_closed.fix: the faulted execution publishes its real partial contribution and the transport row counts only committed bursts

defects_closed.symptom: a faulted execution published an empty transfer while the transport row kept the committed prefix, so the per-execution facts contradicted the accounting row

defects_closed.fix: per-burst payloads are folded over the committed bursts in logical order at completion
defects_closed.root_cause: the digest was folded per burst as it was read or committed
defects_closed.symptom: a descriptor payload digest depended on commit/prepare order and included uncommitted bursts

defects_closed.fix: dma_shapes uses the shared producer-content entry, p2p_reuse verifies per-transfer coverage against the admitted oracle, pin derives the declared fill payload, and cross_core_order was retired in favour of the shared E2E-B ordering check
defects_closed.root_cause: the checks were written before the admitted execution model and never re-derived
defects_closed.symptom: four case oracles failed on stale expectations: dma_shapes compared the P2P payload to the fill pattern, p2p_reuse expected a hardcoded 64 bytes, pin expected a byte-repeated pattern digest, and cross_core_order expected an EVENT_WAIT the program no longer has

defects_closed.fix: arch_digest is the base manifest digest and the effective digest is recorded separately
defects_closed.root_cause: the runner passed the post-override effective digest as the program's base architecture identity
defects_closed.symptom: every architecture-tuning case aborted with E_ARCH_DIGEST

defects_closed.fix: per-byte coverage bitmaps, live-versus-retired lane ownership, duplicate-notification accounting, and published per-transfer coverage facts checked by verified_transfer_publishes
defects_closed.root_cause: expectation coverage was a byte counter with no notion of which byte, which expectation owns it, or whether the notification is a replay
defects_closed.symptom: the peer aperture counted observed bytes instead of tracking coverage: a replayed observer notification inflated committed bytes and could release a transfer before its remaining bytes landed, and a retired expectation kept claiming a reused range so the next transfer absorbed those bytes as duplicates and was never released

defects_closed.fix: TargetSentinels is the single sentinel owner for both real target kinds, sampled before cycle 0 and compared after quiescence; verified_sentinels is the shared predicate and wstrb_sentinels the runner check
defects_closed.root_cause: sentinel sampling existed only on the mock FILL path; the real HBM endpoint and peer apertures had no before-cycle-0 sample
defects_closed.symptom: the real targets had no evidence that bytes a transfer must not touch kept their initial value: WSTRB-disabled lanes, row padding and the unaligned head and tail around a payload were never sampled, and only the payload digest was checked

defects_closed.fix: execution_keys clips each descriptor with min(architecture cap, descriptor cap), matching the engine
defects_closed.root_cause: fault_plan clipped bursts with the architecture cap only, while the engine clips with the smaller of the architecture cap and the descriptor cap
defects_closed.symptom: the derived accepted-transaction order under-counted bursts for any descriptor whose beat cap is below the architecture maximum, so uid-based fault plans could target the wrong transaction

defects_closed.fix: seeded_bytes assembles the row from every covering seed range and fails only on a byte nobody declared
defects_closed.root_cause: the read payload oracle demanded one seed range spanning the whole row
defects_closed.symptom: a read row assembled from several adjacent declared seed ranges was reported as outside the declared seeds

defects_closed.fix: the watchdog's real-progress path re-evaluates the gate while the drain is open, and the progress metric counts credit return, ejection, queued flits and ledger movement
defects_closed.root_cause: checkAllHalted was called from notifyCoreHalted only, and progressSample ignored credit return and flit ejection
defects_closed.symptom: the drain gate had a single evaluation point: it ran only when a core halted, so a gate that failed because of in-flight credits or flits was never retried, and the network itself was invisible to the watchdog's progress metric

defects_closed.fix: a dedicated drain event re-evaluates the gate every core clock edge and the drain-phase watchdog reports the pending owners when progress stalls
defects_closed.root_cause: the gate re-check was scheduled on the watchdog event, which carries the staleness deadline rather than the drain cadence
defects_closed.symptom: the drain gate was only re-evaluated at the watchdog deadline (about 100M ticks later), so a drain that needed the network to empty delayed the exit by the whole watchdog period, and a drain that could never finish ran to the simulation limit instead of being reported

defects_closed.fix: every rejection names its phase, and the diagnostic context carries it next to install_state and installed_cores
defects_closed.root_cause: reportRejection took only the lifecycle stage and the two call sites in startup() shared it
defects_closed.symptom: a rejected admission was indistinguishable from a decode failure: both reported the load stage with no phase, so the structured control could not say where admission refused the program

defects_closed.fix: the fault model names the failed burst plus the admitted per-burst bytes, and every fault plan (pre-commit and post-commit) feeds one resolver, the exit-cause derivation and the shared reconciliation
defects_closed.root_cause: the model carried a burst-prefix byte list instead of naming which burst failed, and both the exit-cause derivation and the fault resolver read only mesh_planned_faults
defects_closed.symptom: the fault model only expressed a leading committed prefix, so a real mid-plan post-commit fault (later bursts commit while an earlier one fails) could not be reconciled, and the runner's error expectation ignored post-commit plans entirely

defects_closed.fix: the check splits cancelled-before-issue (no descriptor work allowed) from cancelled-after-submission (real retired executions preserved), and reports both counts
defects_closed.root_cause: the check treated the command terminal state as proof about the descriptor lifecycle
defects_closed.symptom: the cancellation oracle would have required a cancelled command to have issued no work at all, which is wrong for a command cancelled after submission whose descriptors already ran and retired

defects_closed.fix: the aperture routes its notification through the same dispatcher boundary, so both backends share one injection point
defects_closed.root_cause: the aperture called the receiver core directly while the mock routed through MeshDispatcher::routePeerCommit
defects_closed.symptom: the real path's peer notification bypassed the dispatcher delivery boundary, so the existing receiver-fault hooks had no effect and a wrong-target or dropped notification was silently invisible

defects_closed.fix: a stage is recorded only when the expectation's covered bytes increase, so a replay adds a duplicate count but no stage
defects_closed.root_cause: the stage was recorded whenever an expectation was touched rather than when its coverage grew
defects_closed.symptom: a replayed observer notification for already covered bytes appended a commit stage with unchanged coverage, which would have made the staged evidence claim progress that never happened

defects_closed.fix: one _AXI_DIRECTION_FIELDS table maps each descriptor kind to its byte and burst field for both the execution oracle and the fault model, and a kind that issues no AXI burst is refused explicitly
defects_closed.root_cause: the faulted-execution branch derived its byte and burst fields from "read unless read", while the execution oracle kept its own separate kind-to-field mapping, so descriptor kind 3 was read as a STORE
defects_closed.symptom: a faulted P2P execution was measured on the STORE direction's fields, so every real P2P target fault failed reconciliation with "committed 0 bytes over 0 bursts" even though the peer aperture had landed the surviving bursts

defects_closed.fix: an errored instance retires its live expectations as abandoned (PeerSramAperture::abandonAllExpectations): the drain gate stops waiting, the coverage stays reportable, and verified_transfer_publishes requires the receiver's landed bytes and transactions to equal the source's partial contribution while neither side reports a release
defects_closed.root_cause: cancelAllExpectations dropped the expectation table, which owned both the drain-gate liveness and the coverage evidence
defects_closed.symptom: an instance error cleared every peer expectation, so the coverage a partially committed transfer had really landed disappeared from the archived aperture facts and a partially committed transfer was indistinguishable from one that was never armed

defects_closed.fix: the five stale imports name mesh_ir.architecture and the selector reads the verified field; the manifest authority test no longer resolves the interpreter symlink, which had dropped the locked venv's site-packages and made the child fail on its own imports
defects_closed.root_cause: the frontend restructuring moved load_arch to mesh_ir.architecture and replaced Program.semantic_sha256() with a verified string field, but the selector and the arch unit tests were left on the old API
defects_closed.symptom: four Gate 1/Gate 2 architecture unit modules and two manifest-selector integration modules could not even be collected: they still imported load_arch from mesh_ir.builder, and the checked-in manifest selector still called Program.semantic_sha256() as a method

defects_closed.fix: a repeated installation of the same admitted range set states the same expectation and is idempotent; a different range set for one transfer is still refused
defects_closed.root_cause: the sender arms a transfer once per admitted descriptor it submits while PeerSramAperture::expectTransfer treated any second installation as a hard error
defects_closed.symptom: any admitted multi-descriptor P2P transfer aborted the real path with "transfer 1 expected twice": every existing carrier had exactly one P2P descriptor per transfer, so the arming path was never exercised more than once

defects_closed.fix: the real engine indexes the pattern by the payload-wide offset, so both backends expand one admitted fill payload
defects_closed.root_cause: the real engine expanded the 64-bit pattern from byte 0 at every row while the mock engine and fill_pattern_bytes expand it across the whole descriptor payload
defects_closed.symptom: a multi-row LOCAL_FILL whose row_bytes is not a multiple of eight filled a different pattern on the real path than on the mock path and the shared oracle, so the fill payload digest could not reconcile

defects_closed.fix: the real engine records its own commit observation per committed P2P descriptor and reads the destination through MeshDispatcher::readFunctional, which resolves an endpoint address to the SRAM aperture that holds it
defects_closed.root_cause: the per-commit destination record was wired into the mock engine only, and the real engine never implemented the DmaEngineBase readFunctional contract for local or peer endpoint addresses
defects_closed.symptom: a real transfer archived no per-commit destination evidence at all: transfer_commits stayed empty because only the mock engine recorded it, and the observation-only functional read the record needs was unimplemented on the real engine, so it silently returned false

defects_closed.fix: MeshDummyCore::notifyPeerCommit defers to the expectation owner: when a peer aperture holds the transfer's expectation only its own observed commit releases the receiver, and a replayed delivery is recorded as the receiver's own duplicate diagnostic
defects_closed.root_cause: both owners notified on the real path, because the source side never learned that a real peer aperture had taken ownership of the release
defects_closed.symptom: a completed real P2P transfer notified its receiver twice, once from the sender's retirement accounting and once from the target's own observed commit, so the receiving core's delivery count was 2 where the lifecycle rules require exactly one release

defects_closed.fix: the oracle clamps every planned sentinel span to the admitted range of its target, so a byte outside the tile is never declared a sentinel
defects_closed.root_cause: the sentinel oracle planned a fixed neighbourhood around every admitted payload without clamping it to the range the target really holds
defects_closed.symptom: an admitted write at the very start of an SRAM tile declared a sentinel span before the tile base, and the target refused it with "span escapes the target memory", aborting the carrier

defects_closed.fix: the dispatcher snapshots every aperture's coverage into the instance frame it archives, the top-level aperture records keep only lifetime counters and sentinels, and the peer, ordering, commit and staged-stage checks iterate the frames with each frame's own coverage and terminal ticks
defects_closed.root_cause: the receiving tile's coverage was exported from its live expectation table at result-writing time, after every instance had re-armed it, and the ordering checks used the cross-instance core summaries instead of the frame's own terminals
defects_closed.symptom: a multi-instance E2E-2 run had no per-frame peer evidence: the result carried one aperture record for the whole program, the peer checks read the last frame only, and the receiver's ordering and commit checks read cumulative core counters, so an earlier frame's transfer could not be verified at all

defects_closed.fix: one shallow configuration owner plus the shared verified_queue_bounds entry: the E2E-1 and E2E-2 chains run under it, and the entry requires the per-frame in-flight descriptor peak to stay within the admitted depth and to reach it, the read window to be filled but never exceeded, every accepted burst to retire exactly once, and measurable source blocking to exist
defects_closed.root_cause: queue evidence was incidental to the read-window carrier instead of an owned contract over the archived per-frame submit/completion intervals and the adapter's accepted/retired burst counts
defects_closed.symptom: the E2E-1/E2E-2 obligations had no shallow-queue carrier, and the only queue evidence in the archive was the read adapter's peak, so a configuration could call itself shallow without any proof that its bounds really bit or that the engine stayed inside them

defects_closed.fix: the core archives the analytic cycle count with each engine plan, and mesh_ir/compute_timing.py is the single offline definition of the model: it derives every admitted command's cycles from its own attribute and the admission dtypes, requires the archived plan to match, requires the engine to end at the tick the model predicts from its issue tick, and requires the per-core cumulative engine statistics to be the admitted sum
defects_closed.root_cause: the analytic engine latency was computed inside the core and never published, and no offline implementation of the admitted cost model existed
defects_closed.symptom: the real path had no compute timing oracle: the archived engine plans carried only begin/end ticks, and the only pinned compute evidence was a recorded cycle constant on the mock path, so a wrong attribute, dtype throughput or engine selection could not be detected

defects_closed.fix: the oracle claims a compute command's result allocation in full, in the tile that owns it, so the declaration never covers a byte an admitted write may produce; the exact runs stay published as the compute output rows
defects_closed.root_cause: admitted_target_spans only modelled DMA descriptor destinations, while the vector, tensor and reduce engines write through admitted views whose exact runs are only observable at runtime
defects_closed.symptom: the sentinel oracle declared a span over bytes a real compute command legitimately writes, so the peer-edge carrier failed closed on a byte the vector engine had produced itself

defects_closed.fix: a test-only credit-drop fault at the real credit-return boundary (OutputUnit::wakeup), armed by the dispatcher when the drain opens; the data path is untouched, so the run halts normally and only the ledger stays unrestored, which is exactly the state the drain phase must report
defects_closed.root_cause: no fault existed at a boundary whose only observer is the drain gate, so the credit-ledger owner was never exercised
defects_closed.symptom: the drain-phase watchdog branch was implemented and wired but no carrier could reach it: every existing fault stalled a core instead, so the run never reached the state where all cores halted and one drain owner was still busy

defects_closed.fix: the rule now requires a local commit exactly when the drained execution moved bytes, and leaves the byte-level claim to the shared reconciliation fault model, which already pins the surviving burst set
defects_closed.root_cause: the rule was written for the first-burst carrier and encoded 'discards every beat' as an invariant, while the engine keeps the bursts that already landed when the fault is later in the plan
defects_closed.symptom: the completion-timing rule rejected a real mid-plan R error: it required an errored LOAD to have no local commit at all, which only holds when the first burst fails

defects_closed.fix: verified_store_destinations (shared) requires the destination digest to equal the payload the last instance's own STORE execution wrote over the whole admitted span; the README-level read content stays owned by the reconciliation read oracle, which drain_deferred and sram_persist now carry
defects_closed.root_cause: the check predated the shared read oracle and the producer content entry, and it re-derived expectations in the runner instead of comparing the archives it already had
defects_closed.symptom: the E2E-1 content check could not detect a wrong store payload: it only required the destination bytes not to be all zero, and it silently skipped every LOAD descriptor whose seed it could not locate, so a corrupted store or an unverifiable load passed

defects_closed.fix: verified_read_window (shared entry) owns the window rules: fill, refill at the first RLAST rather than at the local commit, a bounded ID pool, ID reuse only after its own RLAST, engine peak and every bridge peak equal to the admitted window, accepted AR ticks equal to the accepted bursts and the first credit release equal to the earliest RLAST; check_read_window_slides is a thin wrapper, the dead _expected_digest helper is deleted, and the observation-field review (a1/field-usage-audit.py) shows every key Gate 5 adds has a consumer while the unconsumed leaves in the archived results are present at HEAD
defects_closed.root_cause: the shared reconciliation entries took over the other Gate 5 rules while the sliding window kept a private rule, and the obsolete helper was not deleted together with the rule it served
defects_closed.symptom: the read-window rules stayed a runner-local check that compared no engine-side or credit-side fact, so nothing proved the engine's own peak and AR accepts, every bridge's accounting and the credited ID release described the same window; the E2E-1 content rewrite also left its replaced private digest helper behind

defects_closed.fix: changed_paths() now takes every git-reported path except evidence, build output and object files; gate5_delta compares changed_sources plus the authority's recorded build/AXI_MESH/gem5.opt, so identity.gate5_delta.modified_vs_gate4_authority equals the authority mismatch set exactly (20 paths); the checker's own log is excluded from the evidence hashes because the run it records rewrites it
defects_closed.root_cause: changed_paths() filtered git status by a source-suffix allow-list, which silently drops build inputs without a listed extension; the authority comparison read only changed_sources and never the authority's recorded binary
defects_closed.symptom: identity.changed_sources omitted the extension-less and non-listed sources this work changed (.gitignore, src/dev/ai_mesh/SConscript, src/dev/ai_mesh/generated/golden_mshb.inc, util/mesh_ir/requirements-lock.txt), and the comparison against the Gate 4 authority ignored the recorded model binary, so the checker reported unexplained authority mismatches

defects_closed.fix: the check now asserts only what the shared entry does not own: the admitted instance set, the errored instance's outcome, the healthy instance's complete and isolated ledger, every frame's terminal outcomes and no live command; the duplicate assertion and the local R-beat bound are deleted
defects_closed.root_cause: the check grew while the shared reconciliation entry took over burst and byte accounting, so a duplicated assertion, a redundant instance loop and a partial-plan bound stayed behind
defects_closed.symptom: the first-instance-error check asserted the same live-command rule twice, re-checked instance 1 with a second loop over the same frames, and bounded the run's R beats with a locally re-derived admitted beat plan

defects_closed.fix: verified_post_commit_landing(result, *, admitted_burst_bytes) owns the rule (one errored descriptor, no claimed source commit, destination equals the bytes read from the producer, the target's committed count, exactly the admitted burst failed); the runner wrapper passes the admitted burst size and four corruption cases replay the entry
defects_closed.root_cause: the landing check was written next to its carrier instead of as a shared entry, and the failing span was a literal rather than the admitted burst size
defects_closed.symptom: the post-commit landing rule lived in the runner with a hard-coded 512-byte failing burst, so no section 7 negative could replay it and the rule itself was untestable

defects_closed.fix: verified_burst_geometry takes the admitted (address, beats) pairs and requires the archived bursts to equal them; the runner no longer compares the split itself; a duplicated burst masking a missing one, a write relabelled as a response, a short burst plan claiming completion and a coordinated execution+traffic deletion all replay the shared entries
defects_closed.root_cause: the geometry entry never received the admitted plan, so plan equality stayed a runner-local comparison and the section 7.2/7.3 duplicates could not be replayed through a production entry
defects_closed.symptom: verified_burst_geometry checked only page and beat limits, so the runner compared the admitted AW split itself and a duplicated or relabelled burst had no shared rule and no negative test

defects_closed.fix: util/mesh_ir/tests/unit/test_gate1_package_contract.py is replayed and archived: it builds the current wheel and sdist and asserts the built artifacts carry the current modules, the pinned lock and no work trees (5 passed)
defects_closed.root_cause: the package contract suite stayed in the Gate 1 index and was never replayed against the modules this work added
defects_closed.symptom: section 5.F.2 requires the wheel contract whenever new package modules are added, and the status carried no Gate 5 run of it although this work added mesh_ir modules

defects_closed.fix: peer_transfer_coverage.{hh,cc} owns a single-use (instance, uid) transaction identity and the aperture delegates to it; the real boundary can re-deliver an old commit after the next expectation arms (--replay-peer-commit); verified_transfer_publishes requires complete, disjoint transaction identities and exact refused-replay accounting
defects_closed.root_cause: coverage was attributed by address only; the transaction identity was recorded but never used for ownership
defects_closed.symptom: a replayed old transaction could complete a new transfer that reuses the same address

defects_closed.fix: burst_attribution.hh plus the engine's instance-scoped records archive (instance, core, command, generation, descriptor, burst, ordinal) with response/local-commit/retire/done ticks; verified_burst_attribution pairs them with the admitted plan (registered for every Garnet carrier); delayed_b and the new delayed_b_ejection carrier prove both delay mechanisms
defects_closed.root_cause: burst_timings carried no execution attribution and the per-instance R/B retirement facts were cleared at the instance boundary
defects_closed.symptom: a B response later than every descriptor terminal tick was accepted

defects_closed.fix: the dispatcher archives a per-instance destination read-back per admitted row; verified_destination_bytes proves admitted geometry, producer raw bytes, payload digest and destination raw bytes per instance; registered as destination_bytes on the E2E carriers
defects_closed.root_cause: the STORE entry compared digests only and consumed the last instance only
defects_closed.symptom: the E2E byte contract accepted a changed or missing destination byte

defects_closed.fix: the aperture archives its covered ranges; verified_transfer_snapshots splits a cut-short span byte-exactly into landed producer bytes and admitted initial content, requires a real read-back and that every archived digest is one of the transfer's own landing states
defects_closed.root_cause: the cut_short branch only checked the digest length and skipped the combined pending digest
defects_closed.symptom: a partial-failure destination was exempt from content checks

defects_closed.fix: the result publishes per-vnet cumulative injected/received packets and flits plus the flit width; the loader snapshot carries the same cumulative counters; verified_garnet_traffic reconciles them with the admitted packetizer projection and loader_control_plane_delta requires the complete field set, integer counters, no rollback and an empty delta
defects_closed.root_cause: the result archived only quiescence occupancy and the loader check compared key sets only
defects_closed.symptom: there was no cumulative packet/flit oracle and an empty loader snapshot pair passed

defects_closed.fix: each case publishes its immutable program inputs into a content-addressed store and references it from identity.json/command.json; check_manifest.py reads every referenced file back; the stale slice and cross-gate text is replaced by the current evidence; the duplicated admitted_transfer_* helpers are gone
defects_closed.root_cause: the matrix only hashed a temporary program build dir, and slices/cross-gate text kept gaps that the work had already closed
defects_closed.symptom: the archive was not replayable and the status index carried stale gap text

defects_closed.fix: verified_burst_attribution indexes executions by (core, command, generation, descriptor), requires done_tick == execution completion_tick, bounds issue and handshake by the execution's submit/completion, forbids errored bursts on committed executions, equates a committed execution's archived bursts and moved bytes with its own transfer facts, and anchors every core's archived totals to its bridge counters
defects_closed.root_cause: the burst entry compared each burst's retirement against the terminal tick the burst row itself reported, never against the execution ledger, so a late B could raise its own bound; a burst could name a core that ran no such execution and a healthy committed read could self-report an error to skip its local SRAM commit

defects_closed.fix: every source row's raw bytes must SHA-256 to its archived digest, joining destination bytes, transfer payload, source SHA and producer SHA into one content chain
defects_closed.root_cause: the E2E byte entry trusted the execution's raw source bytes without connecting them to the row digest that the producer-content chain pins to the admitted compute producer, so raw bytes and producer SHA could describe two different physical contents

defects_closed.fix: the coverage table records per-commit landing events (tick, single-use transaction identity, newly covered runs), the runner projects those events onto every snapshot, and verified_transfer_snapshots requires each pending span digest to equal the landing state its events had reached at that row's commit tick
defects_closed.root_cause: partial-failure landing states were projected from the transfer's final coverage, so an early snapshot could borrow a digest a later burst only reaches; the descriptor submit tick stood in for real target commits

defects_closed.fix: verified_garnet_traffic normalizes the expectation over every legal vnet with a zero baseline and compares all of them; the wrapper drops the channel-count gate and packet_traffic became a base invariant of every Garnet carrier
defects_closed.root_cause: the traffic entry only compared vnets the plan used, so extra packets on an unplanned vnet passed, and the wrapper's five-channel requirement excluded pure-read, pure-write and zero-DMA carriers instead of zeroing their expectations

defects_closed.fix: run_case_matrix archives the immutable source map (changed-sources.json) once per run, every case identity references it with path/count/digest and the real pinned environment, and check_manifest validates the map's content, count, binary/config agreement and rejects placeholder environments, with tamper negatives
defects_closed.root_cause: case identities carried only a digest of a source map nobody archived and the recorded environment held undefined placeholders, so the execution identity could not be replayed from the archive

defects_closed.fix: the duplicated block was removed; behaviour is unchanged and the binary was rebuilt
defects_closed.root_cause: an editing leftover duplicated the last_commit_tick assignment and error-drain guard verbatim in PeerSramAperture::observeCommit

defects_closed.fix: verified_burst_attribution now enforces the instance boundary: every burst of frame N+1 must be submitted after the latest completion of frame N, an anchor a within-frame consistent lie cannot move past; verified on all 46 archived cases and a two-instance long-term negative
defects_closed.root_cause: the burst entry anchored every burst to its execution ledger but nothing anchored the ledger itself across instances: a fully coherent time shift of one execution's bursts, its own terminal and the terminal row into the next instance's window passed every internal consistency check

defects_closed.fix: the runner projects (tick, offset, size, uid) events with the transfer's transaction identities and verified_transfer_snapshots requires every nonzero event identity to be one the transfer recorded, at most once; long-term negatives on a real partial-failure run
defects_closed.root_cause: landing events carried their single-use transaction identity but no consumer read it, so a foreign or duplicated identity could explain a pending descriptor's landing

defects_closed.fix: every burst requires a positive request handshake inside submit..completion, and retirement may not precede it; same-tick response and handshake stay legal, delayed B and error-drain semantics unchanged
defects_closed.root_cause: the burst entry bounded retirement by the execution terminal but never from below: a response could retire before its request was even accepted, and a missing handshake tick was treated as a skip

defects_closed.fix: the shared entry now closes the errored execution: its declared successful burst counts equal its non-errored archived bursts, a failing status requires the faulted burst in the right direction, a plan cut by the fault ends on the faulted burst, per-core errored-B responses equal the bridge's error classification and error beats imply errored read bursts
defects_closed.root_cause: an errored execution only had to archive a plan prefix, so the faulted burst or a successful burst could be deleted together with coherent bridge and network counters and every registered check still passed

defects_closed.fix: events are one transaction's timed landing (tick, uid, ranges, request) and the identity budget is transfer-wide: the events this pending span claims plus every landing archived elsewhere must stay inside the recorded identity multiset, zero included
defects_closed.root_cause: landing events carried their transaction identity but a uid of 0 bypassed attribution, and identity multiplicity was never checked, so one recorded identity could explain landings it never made

defects_closed.fix: the projection resolves each event to the accepted write burst covering its ranges and carries that burst's handshake tick; the entry rejects any landing that precedes its request, so the digests of a backdated event can no longer self-certify
defects_closed.root_cause: a landing event's tick proved itself: backdating the event and recomputing every snapshot digest still passed, because nothing tied the event to the request that carried it

defects_closed.fix: admitted_write_identities pairs each accepted write burst with the identity the admitted accept order assigns it, over the burst's own useful span (logical start, not the beat base); every event must claim the identity of the burst whose span carries its ranges, inside that span, and the transfer-wide quota is kept as a second bound
defects_closed.root_cause: the landing-event identity budget proved multiset membership, not association: permuting legal identities between events kept every quota intact and passed every registered check

defects_closed.fix: the request bound comes from the same-transaction accepted burst the event is now associated with, so backdating to its own handshake minus one is rejected regardless of neighbouring requests; digest-consistent backdating no longer self-certifies
defects_closed.root_cause: the landing time lower bound searched every write burst sharing the beat envelope and took the earliest handshake, so a landing could sit before its own request while after an unrelated overlapping one

defects_closed.fix: verified_landing_events validates the transfer's complete raw landing-event set -- completed and pending alike -- against admitted identities, useful-span geometry and same-transaction request handshakes, before any pending timeline is derived; the runner and the tests only prepare inputs (aperture row, admitted write identities, frame bursts, span read-backs) and both former owner_of implementations are deleted
defects_closed.root_cause: the per-event transaction association covered only pending descriptors; events of completed descriptors were reduced to a uid list, so swapping two legal identities or backdating a completed landing before its own request passed every registered check

defects_closed.fix: verified_landing_events now requires each event to carry positive addressed ranges, the event list to pair one-to-one with the receiver's coverage stages at identical ticks and cumulative bytes, and the union of all event ranges to equal the archived covered_ranges and covered_bytes exactly, so any missing or truncated landing fails closed
defects_closed.root_cause: the landing-event entry validated every surviving event but never the completeness of the set: deleting a completed transaction's event, emptying its ranges or shortening a legal range left the archived coverage facts unexplained and passed every registered check

defects_closed.fix: the key set gained the execution ordinal (zero-based, as execution_keys emits it) and the association resolves the owning execution through the frame's generation-ordered execution rows; the REPEAT carrier's three executions now keep three distinct identity groups
defects_closed.root_cause: admitted_write_identities keyed accepted write bursts by (descriptor, instance, burst_index) and discarded execution_keys' execution ordinal, silently collapsing the identities of repeated executions onto the last one

defects_closed.fix: verified_landing_events bounds a landing from above by its own paired burst's write response when that response has arrived (response_tick > 0): the target adapter invokes the commit observer before building and queueing the B, so a fresh landing cannot postdate its own response; bursts still waiting for a response carry response_tick == 0 and get no upper bound, so undrained diagnostics and post-commit error landings keep their semantics; same-tick landing and response stay legal
defects_closed.root_cause: the landing-event time window had a lower bound (its own request handshake) but no upper bound: moving an event and its stage together to a tick after the transaction's own B response and retirement still passed every registered check, because the two self-consistent tick fields could lie together
